speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with your age and when you first noticed the swelling in your right knee. Does the swelling come and go, or is it constant? Also, do you have any family members with a history of joint replacements or severe arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia (likely A or B) presenting with spontaneous hemarthrosis. Given the patient's age, trauma-free onset, and family history, bleeding disorders must be ruled out immediately. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, PTT), Factor VIII and IX levels.
